patients.summary: Healthy construction foreman who joined in August 2024. Trichinellosis after eating campfire-grilled game meat in July 2025 (ED, albendazole, resolved), then a new infection from undercooked fair pork in June 2026 needing a short admission; records from outside care arrive late.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller would like to move his primary care to us. Age 33, works as a foreman for a construction outfit, says he hasn't had a real checkup in a few years. Employer PPO, card info entered. Reviewed membership and how to reach the doctor by text. New patient physical booked 8/20 at 8:00 so he can get to the site after. Release signed over the phone for records from his previous primary care office; request faxed today.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Records received by fax, 11 pages, covering 2016 through 2021.

Patient last seen there for a physical in 2021. No chronic problems on their list. Past surgical: tonsillectomy in childhood. Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Immunizations on file: childhood series documented; Td 2012. Influenza vaccines in some years.
Labs from 2021: CBC and metabolic panel unremarkable; lipids within normal range.

Scanned to chart. No action items.

documents.title: New Patient Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
33M here to set up primary care. Last physical about three years ago at his old office, records reviewed. Feels well. No complaints today. Runs crews for a commercial builder, on his feet all day, sleeps ok, gets the usual sore back on long pour days but nothing persistent.

PMH: none.
PSH: tonsils out as a kid (about age 8).
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: dad with type 2 DM. Mom on thyroid replacement for hypothyroidism. One sibling, healthy.
Social: never smoked. Beer on weekends, 3-4 a week. No drugs. Single, lives in town.

ROS negative across the board.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Well appearing, muscular. HEENT normal, oropharynx clear, tonsils absent. Neck supple, no thyromegaly or nodes. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Skin without rashes, no concerning moles. Ext no edema, full ROM. Neuro grossly normal. PHQ-2 0.

A/P: healthy adult, preventive visit.
- Labs: CBC, CMP, lipids. A1c given dad's diabetes. One-time HCV and HIV screens, he agrees.
- Last tetanus was 2012 per old records, Tdap given today (he works around rebar and nails).
- Flu and covid shots when they come in this fall.
- Sunscreen at work, hearing protection around equipment.
RTC one year.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Glenn, everything from Tuesday came back fine. Blood counts, kidney and liver tests normal, cholesterol in a good range, A1c normal so no sign of diabetes, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. Nothing to change. Good to meet you.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In before work for flu and covid. Denies fever or illness today, no prior vaccine reactions. Flu vaccine L deltoid, covid R deltoid. Waited 15 minutes in the lobby, no issues, left for his job site.

documents.title: Shot record for work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: New general contractor on our current job wants proof of tetanus for everybody on site. Can you send me something showing the one I got in August?

documents.title: RE: Shot record for work
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Glenn, your immunization record is attached in the portal under Documents. It shows the Tdap from 8/20/2024 along with your fall flu and covid vaccines. Let us know if they need it on a specific form.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (400 mg) by mouth twice daily with food for 10 days

documents.title: Was in the ER
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Ended up in the ER last night. Been achy all over with fevers for about 5 days and my eyes swelled up. They think it's a worm/parasite from the meat we cooked on the hunting trip a couple weeks ago. Gave me a pill to take twice a day for 10 days. Do you want to see me? I'm off site till Monday anyway.

documents.title: RE: Was in the ER
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad you went in. That fits with trichinella, which comes from undercooked game. Finish every dose of the albendazole and take it with food. Fluids, rest, Tylenol for the aches is fine. Come in Tuesday morning and we'll check blood work and see how the swelling is doing. If you get short of breath, chest pain, or the weakness gets worse, go back to the ER.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED f/u. Seen in a regional ED 7/2 for 5 days of fever, myalgias and periorbital swelling. Back from an out-of-state hunting trip about two weeks before that; the group cooked game over a campfire and some of it was underdone by his account. Felt ok for a few days after getting home, then low fevers and a vague crampy belly, then the muscle aches and puffy eyes. ED told him presumed trichinella and started albendazole 400 bid x10 days. We do not have the ED record yet, requested today.

Now day 6 of albendazole, taking with food, no GI upset. No fever since Saturday. Thighs and shoulders still sore climbing ladders but better each day. Eye swelling mostly gone in the mornings. No SOB, chest pain, palpitations, rash or trouble swallowing.

Exam: afebrile, vitals reviewed. Mild puffiness of both lower lids. Conjunctivae clear. Heart RRR no murmur, lungs clear. Mild tenderness of both anterior thighs, strength 5/5 throughout. No rash. Nails normal.

A/P: trichinellosis, improving on treatment.
- CBC with diff, CK, and trichinella antibody to confirm.
- finish albendazole.
- light duty this week if he can, note given.
- recheck in about a month with repeat CBC/CK.
- counseled: game meat and pork cooked through, freezing doesn't reliably kill the wild-game strains.

documents.title: Results from Tuesday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glenn, the trichinella antibody came back positive, so that confirms what the ER thought. Your eosinophils (the white cells that react to parasites) are still up at 1.4 and the muscle enzyme CK is 310, a bit above normal. Both are what I'd expect a week into treatment and should drift down. Finish the pills, and let's recheck in about a month.

documents.title: RE: Results from Tuesday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks doc. Feeling a lot better already. Will book for August.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record, regional hospital, visit 07/02/2025
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 07/02/2025

CC: myalgias, fevers and swelling around both eyes x5 days.

HPI: 34 yo male, healthy. Returned about two weeks ago from an out-of-state hunting trip where he ate game meat grilled over an open fire. Asymptomatic initially. About 3 days after returning developed low-grade fevers and mild nonspecific abdominal discomfort, followed over the last several days by progressive diffuse muscle aching, fatigue and periorbital puffiness. Denies cough, sore throat, sick contacts.

PMH: none. PSH: tonsillectomy age 8. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father T2DM, mother hypothyroidism, sibling healthy.
SH: never smoker; 3-4 drinks/week socially; construction foreman.

Triage: T 38.3 C (101 F), BP 118/72, HR 92.

Exam: nontoxic. Bilateral periorbital edema. Thighs and upper arms tender to palpation. Lungs clear, heart regular. Abdomen soft, nontender. No rash.

Labs: CBC with leukocytosis and eosinophilia. CK mildly elevated.

MDM: fever, myositis picture, periorbital edema and eosinophilia after undercooked wild game; presumed trichinellosis.

Disposition: discharged home. Albendazole 400 mg PO BID x10 days. Antipyretics as needed. Follow up with PCP within 1 week; return for chest pain, dyspnea or weakness.

Filed 7/24. PCP note: already seen 7/8, antibody confirmed.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Recheck after trichinella in July. Finished all 10 days of albendazole. Back to full duty for 3 weeks, no aches, no fevers, eyes back to normal. Appetite fine.

Exam: well. No periorbital edema. No muscle tenderness, strength full. Heart and lungs normal. Skin clear.

CBC with diff and CK drawn this morning, resulted before he left: WBC 7.2, eos 4% (0.3), CK 140. All normal now.

A/P: trichinellosis, resolved. Taking it off the active list. Talked again about cooking any wild game and pork all the way through, he says the hunting group has already heard about it from him. No further labs needed. See him for his physical in the fall.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu and covid for this season. Feeling well, no fever. Last year's shots gave him a sore arm only. Flu L arm, covid R arm, lot numbers in the immunization record. Observed 15 min without reaction.

documents.title: Reschedule
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt can't make 10/21 at 7:30, concrete delivery moved up. Moved to Tues 11/4 at 7:30. Reminded him to come fasting.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
34M for yearly physical. Feeling good. Busy season wrapping up, a couple of 60-hour weeks in September, now easing. No lingering muscle problems since the trichinella in July, which resolved. No new symptoms.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: unchanged. Never smoker, a few beers a week.
FH unchanged (dad DM2, mom hypothyroid).

ROS: negative.

Exam: well, vitals reviewed. HEENT normal. No thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. Skin with no rashes or worrisome lesions, some sun on forearms. Muscles nontender, strength normal. No edema. PHQ-2: 1.

A/P: well adult.
- CBC and CMP today. Lipids and A1c were fine last year, will repeat A1c next year given his dad.
- Flu and covid done 10/7. Tdap current (2024).
- Back next fall, or text me sooner.

documents.title: Labs from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All normal, Glenn. Blood counts, kidneys, liver and sugar all where they should be. See you next year.

documents.title: It's back I think
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Doc, my eyes are puffy again like last summer and I'm sore all over, worse every day this week. Now I've got a rash too. Haven't been hunting. Can you see me?

documents.title: RE: It's back I think
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes. Come in at 7:30 tomorrow, I'll fit you in before my first patient. If you get short of breath or chest pain tonight, go to the ER instead.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

orders.reason: trichinellosis with fever, rash and splinter hemorrhages

documents.title: Acute Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen urgently. Had trichinella last July from hunting-trip game, treated and cleared with normal labs in August.

Now: about three weeks ago had a couple of days of belly pain with nausea and vomiting that passed on its own, he chalked it up to a bug. Over the past week progressively sore muscles, legs and arms, eyes swelling again, and a rash that spread over the trunk and limbs in the last few days. Fevers at home. No travel this year, no hunting. When asked about food, he ate a pulled pork sandwich at a fair about two weeks before the stomach trouble and remembers it being pink in the middle. No SOB, chest pain or palpitations. Taking nothing but Tylenol.

Exam: T 38.3, other vitals in flowsheet. Looks tired. Bilateral periorbital edema. Diffuse rash over trunk and extremities. Splinter hemorrhages under several fingernails. Tender to palpation over thighs, calves and upper arms. Heart regular, no murmur heard. Lungs clear.

A/P: picture is trichinellosis again, a new infection from the fair pork, not a relapse of last year's. More systemic this time with the rash and nail findings, and febrile. Splinter hemorrhages fit trichinella but with fever I want cultures before calling it. Talked with the hospitalist at the regional hospital, accepted for direct admission today: labs, cultures, start treatment and steroids per them. A friend from his crew is driving him straight over.
I'll follow along.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (400 mg) by mouth twice daily with food for 14 days
Take 2 tablets (40 mg) by mouth once daily for 7 days

documents.title: Outside fill notification
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Fill history feed shows two new fills on 6/26 from a hospital prescriber: albendazole 200 mg tabs, 2 tabs twice daily x14 days (#56), and prednisone 20 mg tabs, 2 tabs daily x7 days (#14). Looks like discharge meds. No discharge paperwork here yet. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Home
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got out Friday. Fever's gone, eyes better, rash fading. Still sore. They gave me the same worm pills for 2 weeks and steroids for a week. Back at work light duty Monday.

documents.title: RE: Home
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good to hear. Finish both prescriptions. Once the albendazole is done, book a visit with me so we can recheck your blood counts and muscle enzyme and look at those fingernails. Front desk can set it up, or text me a day that works with your schedule.

documents.title: RE: Home
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Will do once things calm down on the job.

documents.title: Hospital records request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Still no discharge summary from the 6/23-6/26 admission. Called the hospital's medical records line, request for discharge summary and labs faxed with the release on file. They quoted 2-3 weeks.

documents.title: Discharge Summary, regional hospital, admitted 06/23/2026
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - MEDICINE SERVICE
Admission: 06/23/2026   Discharge: 06/26/2026
Referred by: primary care, direct admission.

Principal diagnosis: Trichinellosis (new infection; prior episode 2025 from wild game, treated).

History: 35 yo male, sent in by his PCP. Roughly three weeks of illness beginning with abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting that settled without treatment, then one week of progressive myalgias, periorbital swelling and a diffuse rash. No recent travel. Ate undercooked pork at a local fair about two weeks before the GI symptoms began. No home medications. NKDA. PSH tonsillectomy age 8. FH father DM2, mother hypothyroidism, sibling healthy. Never smoker, 3-4 drinks/week, construction foreman.

On admission: T 38.3 C. Periorbital edema; muscles tender on palpation; subungual splinter hemorrhages; diffuse rash.

Admission labs: WBC 12,000/mm3; Hgb 14 g/dL; eosinophils 2,000/mm3 (16%); CK 600 U/L (ref 38-174); ALT 45 U/L (ref 7-56); AST 50 U/L (ref 8-48). Blood cultures x2: no growth at 5 days.

Hospital course: started albendazole 400 mg twice daily and prednisone 40 mg daily. Defervesced by hospital day 2, myalgias and eyelid swelling improving, tolerating diet, ambulating independently. Discharged home on hospital day 4.

Discharge medications:
- albendazole 400 mg PO BID, to complete 14 days
- prednisone 40 mg PO daily, to complete 7 days

Follow-up: PCP in 2-3 weeks with CBC with differential and CK. Return for chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations or worsening weakness.

Received by fax 8/11. Filed to chart.
